title: Suresh Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Shekhar B. Saraf, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner directed to apply under Clause 6.5.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash a current electricity bill is disposed of by directing the consumer to file an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If filed within two weeks, the authority shall hear the consumer and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks.
facts: Suresh Singh filed a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution seeking to quash a current electricity bill issued by respondent no.5 for the period 3 October 2024 to 2 November 2024, demanding Rs.11,396. Counsel for the State and for respondent nos. 2 to 5 were heard. The Court did not examine whether the bill was correctly raised and treated the grievance as one for the billing-objection machinery under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.holding: A consumer who approaches the High Court to quash a current electricity bill is directed to file an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if that application is filed within two weeks, the authority shall grant a hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks.

not_decided.point: Validity of the current bill dated 3.10.2024 to 2.11.2024 for Rs.11,396
not_decided.note: Merits of the bill were not examined; the petitioner was relegated to Clause 6.5.
